campbell.title: Campbell City Council — July 7, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered renewing an interim ordinance related to state Senate Bill implementation, along with two separate hearings on revoking the business license and tobacco retailer permit for California Cigar and for Hayes Smoke Shop. The council also considered authorizing a grant application for public works funding and approving new consultant service agreements.
keyTopics: Renewal of an interim ordinance implementing a state Senate Bill
Revocation of business license and tobacco retailer permit for California Cigar
Revocation of business license and tobacco retailer permit for Hayes Smoke Shop
Authorization to submit a grant application through the Public Works Department
Approval of consultant service agreements

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — May 20, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council considered a resolution declaring the City's intent to identify properties that fall under a designated assessment or district program. The Council also planned to set a public hearing for June 17, 2026, where property owners could raise protests before the Council considers final approval.
keyTopics: Resolution declaring intent to identify designated properties
Process for property owners to file protests
Scheduling of the June 17, 2026 public hearing
Steps toward final approval of the property designation

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — August 4, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council considered routine administrative and contract items, including approving minutes from prior meetings and several contract amendments covering tree care services, legal services, and library book purchases. The council also reviewed the town's monthly financial and investment report.
keyTopics: Approval of minutes from the June 16 and June 23, 2026 council meetings
Contract amendment with Brightview Tree Care for tree maintenance services
Fifth amendment to the town's legal services contract
Purchase of library books and materials from Ingram for the coming fiscal year
Monthly financial and investment report review

san-jose.title: San José City Council — August 11, 2026
san-jose.summary: The San José City Council met to handle routine business, including approving previous City Council and committee meeting minutes and making appointments to various committees, boards, and commissions. The Council also considered general authorization for airport grants and a proposed amendment to the city's Deferred Compensation Plan for employees.
keyTopics: Approval of prior City Council and committee meeting minutes
Council appointments to committees, boards, and commissions
General authorization for airport-related grants
Amendment to the City of San José Deferred Compensation Plan

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — June 23, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View City Council met to handle several honorary proclamations, including recognition of National Immigrant Heritage Month, the Kiwanis Club's 100th anniversary, and City Attorney Jennifer Logue's appointment to the judiciary. The Council also considered a closed-session discussion on potential litigation, set the city's spending limit for the coming fiscal year, updated financial and water-management policies, reviewed the capital improvement program, and took up several public works project items including the Public Safety Building, Shoreline Golf Links parking lot repaving, and the South Bay Salt Pond Restoration project.
keyTopics: Closed-session discussion on anticipated litigation (2 potential cases)
Proclamations for Immigrant Heritage Month, the Kiwanis Club's 100th anniversary, and City Attorney Jennifer Logue's judicial appointment
Fiscal Year 2026-27 appropriations limit and updates to the city's financial and budgetary policy
5-Year Update to the Urban Water Management Plan and Water Shortage Contingency Plan
Capital improvement projects, including the Public Safety Building, Shoreline Golf Links parking lot repaving, and South Bay Salt Pond Restoration

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — July 28, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council held a late-afternoon closed session followed by a study session focused on the city's artificial turf policy. During the study session, council members reviewed an update on how artificial turf is being considered or regulated within the city, though no formal action was taken at this meeting.
keyTopics: Closed session discussion
Update on the city's Artificial Turf Policy
Review of considerations around artificial turf use in Sunnyvale

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — August 4, 2026
cupertino.summary: This Cupertino City Council meeting agenda covered standard procedural items, including postponements and the order of business for the day. The agenda set aside time for residents to speak on topics not otherwise listed for discussion, with a structured public comment period.
keyTopics: Postponements and orders of the day
Public oral communications for non-agenda items
Time limits on public speakers (3 minutes each, 30 minutes total)
Opportunity for additional public comment after the City Manager's report

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara Station Area Task Force — July 16, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The Santa Clara Station Area Task Force met on July 16, 2026, with the published agenda mainly covering standard legal disclosures about how residents could challenge certain city decisions. The agenda item highlighted explains the legal deadlines for filing lawsuits against quasi-adjudicative decisions made by the city, rather than detailing specific station area planning proposals.
keyTopics: Standard meeting disclosures on legal appeal deadlines
90-day filing limit under Code of Civil Procedure Section 1094.6
Procedures for challenging city quasi-adjudicative decisions
Station Area Task Force meeting procedures

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — August 3, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council considered a resolution to place a Business Tax Modernization Measure on an upcoming ballot for voters to decide. The proposal would shift the city's business tax structure to a gross receipts model, where taxes are based more directly on a business's actual economic activity, with protections aimed at the roughly 85% of Milpitas businesses that have smaller annual revenues.
keyTopics: Resolution to submit a Business Tax Modernization Measure to voters
Shift to a gross receipts tax structure tied to business revenue
Protections for small businesses with lower annual gross receipts
Comparing Milpitas's business tax revenue to other cities in the region
Simplifying the tax system with tiered rates for administrative clarity

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto City Council — June 29, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto City Council held a public hearing on a proposal for 2468 South Court, where the owner wants to tear down an existing one-story house and detached garage and build a new two-story single-family home with a basement. The Council reviewed a City staff decision (a 'Director's Review') on the project's design and site plan, since a neighbor or interested party appealed that decision for Council reconsideration.
keyTopics: Proposal to demolish an existing house and garage at 2468 South Court
Plans for a new 2,481-square-foot two-story home with a 1,512-square-foot basement
Review of a Junior Accessory Dwelling Unit (JADU) shown in the plans, though it isn't part of this discretionary approval
Appeal of a staff-level 'Director's Review' decision on the project
Confirmation that the project qualifies for a standard environmental review exemption
